name: When Should You Seal a New Driveway?

mainEntity.name: Should I seal my driveway after installation, and when should a contractor do it?
mainEntity.text: Should I seal my driveway after installation, and when should a contractor do it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sealing is often a smart maintenance step, but it is not the same for every driveway material. Concrete may benefit from a sealer after proper curing, especially if the owner wants better stain resistance and easier cleaning. Asphalt typically follows its own sealing schedule, while pavers may need polymeric sand or a protective sealer depending on the finish and usage. In Los Angeles County, sun exposure and occasional rain can make surface protection more valuable over time. The contractor should tell the homeowner when sealing is appropriate, what product is being used, and how often maintenance may be needed. It is important not to seal too early, especially on new concrete, because trapped moisture can affect performance and appearance. If sealing is included in the project, the estimate should state the timing clearly. If it is optional, the contractor should explain the benefits and tradeoffs so the homeowner can decide whether the added cost is worthwhile.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sealing can help protect some driveway surfaces from staining, weathering, and wear, but the timing depends on the material. New concrete usually needs curing time before sealing, while pavers and asphalt have different maintenance schedules. A contractor should explain whether sealing is optional or strongly recommended for the specific surface.
